messages:
maya: Heads-up — saw a 18% drop in prefix/KV cache hit-rate starting after the kernel/attn-tiling rollout at 07:21 UTC. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/boards/attn-kv

jonas: Confirmed on prod traces. p50 ok, but p95/p99 tokens/sec worse and warmup hit-rate for long prompts down ~30%.

priyanka: Uploaded the two comparison graphs (pre vs post): https://dash.redwood/boards/prefix-hit-compare. Looks correlated with the attn kernel flag `attn.tile_size=64` that landed in the runtime.

ryan: Do we have a small repro? Could be key hashing change or just eviction due to slightly different batching. Can we diff raw KV keys emitted by model call across versions?

kelsey: I ran a synthetic sweep against the same prompt set with both runtimes. Quick output:
```
# old runtime: hit_rate=0.82, avg_keys=1024
# new runtime: hit_rate=0.56, avg_keys=1008
# sample key mismatch: hash_old=0x7f3a2b, hash_new=0x4c1d8e
```
This suggests some keys are being produced differently, not just eviction.

anil: Noted one notable change in the attn tiling kernel: we zero-pad KV blocks to align tiles. That padding used to be trimmed before hashing, but a recent compile path bypassed the normal canonicalization. Also: the quant profile tweak (int8-stats) changed ordering of some small-float values near zero. Combine both and you get different byte sequences to hash.

maya: That matches the flamegraphs where we see mismatched cache misses immediately after the first attention window for many sessions. The time series shows cold misses spike at ~token 8 instead of warming by token 4.

jonas: Possible mitigations: (a) re-enable canonical trim for padding in the kernel hot path; (b) add a runtime-key-normalizer that strips trailing zeros and applies canonical quant rounding before hashing; (c) roll back the kernel change. Which is fastest?

priyanka: Rollback is fastest to return hit-rate but blocks the attn tiling perf gains. Runtime normalizer PR is low-risk and can ship as a hotfix. I threw together a prototype that normalizes keys: strips trailing 64-bit zero words and quant-snap to nearest quant bin before hash. Local bench shows hit-rate recovered to ~0.79.

ryan: Can you paste the normalizer snippet?

priyanka: Sure — prototype snippet:
```
// pseudo
bytes normalize_kv(bytes raw) {
  // trim trailing full-zero 64-bit words inserted by tiling
  while (raw.size() >= 8 && raw.ends_with(\"\\x00\\x00\\x00\\x00\\x00\\x00\\x00\\x00\")) raw.truncate(raw.size()-8);
  // apply quant bin snapping to reduce noise from int8 reordering
  for (i=0; i<raw.size(); ++i) raw[i] = quant_snap(raw[i], profile_id);
  return raw;
}
```
This regained most hits in the synthetic.

kelsey: Nice. Two quick asks: (1) add a fast-path check so we only normalize for kernels that set `tile_padding=true` to avoid perf overhead for unaffected models; (2) add unit tests comparing pre/post produced keys for all model variants.

anil: Agreed. Also double-check vector alignment assumptions — some GPUs were optimizing stores and that changed byte ordering for certain widths. Might need an explicit memcopy with defined endianness before hashing.

maya: Can ops-bot annotate the deploy that rolled the tiling kernel? Need exact deploy id/time for rollback decision.

deploy-bot: deploy:runtime-v3.4.7 rolled by @ci at 2024-11-08T07:21:12Z (sha: a1b2c3d). Links: https://deploys.redwood/runtime-v3.4.7

jonas: Plan proposal: ship runtime normalizer behind feature flag (runtime.key_normalize=true) as hotfix to prod, smoke test for 2h, then iterate kernel patch to avoid extra memcopy. If normalizer behaves, keep tiling kernel. If not, rollback v3.4.7.

maya: I'll open an ops-runbook and assign tasks. Priyanka/Kelsey — can you prepare the PR and perf bench? Ryan/Anil — internal kernel patch to reintroduce canonical trim in compile path.

priyanka: PR draft: https://git.redwood/p/rw/runtime/+/2345 — feature-flagged key normalizer + unit tests. Bench results in PR description.

kelsey: I'll run canary on dedicated pool after PR lands. If we see >15% hit-rate regression on canary, abort.

maya: Thanks all. Logging follow-ups here and will ping infra for a quick canary window. :thumbsup:

jonas: One more note — update our perf monitors to report normalized_hit_rate (post-normalizer) so we can see when the flag is on/off in metrics.

priyanka: Added a dashboard to the PR: https://dash.redwood/boards/normalized-hit-rate

maya: Closing the loop — target roll tomorrow EOD unless rollback required.
